# Kspec Automation Session - Task Work

**Session ID:** `01KJKCGRAVN1BTZ611MX7EK5H3`
**Iteration:** 1 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)


### Current State

> **Truncated** (104281 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
$kspec-task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

      "content": "Implementation notes:\n\n1. src/ralph/subagent.ts:\n   - Add formatCompactSection(data, label, fetchCmd) — always returns compact format (identity fields via existing compactSummary() + CLI fetch command). No JSON fence.\n   - Change buildSubagentPrompt to use formatCompactSection instead of formatJsonSection. Keep truncatePromptIfNeeded as final guardrail.\n   - Lower SUBAGENT_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES to 16KB and add WORKER_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES (32KB). Export both.\n\n2. src/cli/commands/ralph.ts:\n   - buildTaskWorkPrompt uses WORKER_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES (32KB) — no behavior change for worker prompts.\n   - Pass explicit maxBytes to truncatePromptIfNeeded call.\n\n3. tests/ralph.test.ts:\n   - Update buildSubagentPrompt tests: assert compact summaries (no json fence for task/spec), always include CLI fetch commands.\n   - Add test: subagent prompt with 37-AC spec stays compact and well under 16KB.\n   - Update budget constant tests.\n   - Add worker prompt test: verify it uses 32KB budget (no regression from constant split).\n   - Existing truncatePromptIfNeeded and formatJsonSection tests stay unchanged (worker path still uses them).",

    }
